_comment: Machine-readable mirror of the premise table in README.md (S-0, frozen 2026-08-21). The README is the document of record; this file exists so harnesses consume premises structurally instead of parsing markdown. Allocation rule: replicate r of cell <id> uses premises[r-1] for every leg.

premises: Miri looks after the school's three hens for the holiday week, and one morning the smallest hen is missing.
Tomas and his grandmother build a kite for the spring festival, but the wind keeps changing and every new design needs testing.
On the first snowy day, Priya must find her little brother's boot, lost somewhere along the sled run, before their walk home.
The class garden's giant pumpkin has a mysterious nibbler, and Sam wants to find out who it is without scaring any animal away.
The town's old carousel breaks a week before the fete, and Nell, the mechanic's apprentice, thinks she can fix it if she can find the missing part.
While shelving returns, library volunteer Theo finds a fifty-year-old letter tucked in an atlas, addressed to someone who still lives in town.
A spring tide strands a rockpool full of creatures far up the beach, and Jonah's tide-watching club has one afternoon to move them safely.
The school orchestra's tuba goes missing on tour day, and Ada traces the mix-up across the town's three delivery vans.
The neighbourhood street market loses its permit spot, and Rosa organizes the stallholders to find and win a new one before Saturday.
An old footpath to the river has been fenced off, and twins Leo and June set out to prove the right of way still exists by walking its forgotten course.
A storm blows a racing pigeon with a numbered leg-ring into Amir's yard, and he sets out to return it to an owner three villages away.
Great-aunt Bee's famous chutney recipe is half missing, and the family kitchen becomes a test lab to reconstruct it before the county show.
A junk-shop chess set turns out to have one piece too many, carved differently from the rest, and Wren traces where the extra piece began.
Two nights before opening, the school play's lead quits, and stage manager Cass must re-plan the show around who is left.
At the harvest swap-market, Idris discovers the tokens everyone trades with have two subtly different mintings, and prices are quietly drifting apart.
The river-gauge readings Dara's science club submits stop matching the town's official numbers, and finding out why means walking the whole river.
